tasks.title: plan_version platform_writes: workspace-inherited Cargo version (fixture-constructed) + multiple platform siblings
tasks.reasoning: AMENDED (corrected AC-002b, spec revision_note): TASK-3's lambda-implementer confirmed via walk.rs:199 (IdentityIndex.platform registration gated to `if *eco == Ecosystem::Npm`, no Cargo branch) plus an empirical real-pipeline run that no Cargo.toml can become a GroupMember::PlatformManifest through real, disk-discovered workspace walk today -- a Cargo platform sibling with `version.workspace = true` resolves as an ordinary GroupMember::Package instead. The corrected AC-002b (read verbatim from the spec file, not paraphrased) now verifies plan_version's OpenContext/workspace-inheritance resolution logic directly against a FIXTURE-CONSTRUCTED GroupMember::PlatformManifest: load a real Workspace via Workspace::load, then push a PlatformManifest member directly into ws.config.groups.fixed's GroupDef.members, bypassing walk.rs discovery entirely. The fixture's `role` field must be set to ManifestRole::Platform{..} (mirroring exactly what walk.rs:213-216 stores for a real npm platform manifest) so the test is falsifiable against AC-002's 'ManifestRole::Canonical unconditionally, regardless of the member's own role field' clause -- an implementation that forwarded member.role into ManifestDecl::new instead of hardcoding Canonical would hit the Platform-role-vs-CargoToml-format rejection at callisto-model/src/package.rs:104-106 and fail this test. The owner Package member must receive a real PlannedBump this run (not left unbumped), since AC-002b's own text notes the criterion is otherwise vacuously satisfiable per AC-006. Verified via direct read of the currently landed commands/version.rs (lines 261-334, commits 431feb9 + c3516ba): the platform_writes loop already iterates `group.members(GroupMemberKind::PlatformManifest)` generically -- it has no dependency on how the member entered `ws.config.groups.fixed` (real walk discovery vs. direct fixture construction) -- and already hardcodes `ManifestRole::Canonical` in the `ManifestDecl::new` call at line 300, ignoring the member's own `role` field, and already derives `cargo_workspace`/`open_ctx` from the real workspace root (lines 264-280). So this fixture-based AC-002b test requires zero further implementation changes; it is written purely to pin the behavior AC-002b now describes. AC-007 (unaffected by the correction, confirmed already satisfied by TASK-2's landed producer loop) keeps its original real-discovery test content unchanged, verbatim, per the spec revision_note's own statement that AC-007 required no change.

test.description: Two tests. AC-002b [REWRITTEN per corrected spec]: fixture-constructed GroupMember::PlatformManifest -- build a real Workspace via Workspace::load (a Cargo owner package plus a separate, ordinary, non-grouped Cargo package acting as the fixture's on-disk platform manifest target), then push a `crate::config::groups::GroupMember::PlatformManifest` literal directly into `ws.config.groups.fixed`'s matching `GroupDef.members`, with `role: callisto_model::ManifestRole::Platform { platform, arch, abi }` set (not default/unpinned) and `path` pointing at a Cargo.toml declaring `version.workspace = true`, whose workspace root `[workspace.package] version` is a distinct, recognizable value ("3.2.1"). The owner Package member must receive a real PlannedBump this run (via a changeset targeting the owner). Call plan_version(&ws, ..) and assert Ok(..) with platform_writes containing exactly one entry: manifest == the fixture path, from == "3.2.1" (the resolved workspace-inherited version, not an Err(ManifestError::WorkspaceInherited) and not missing/empty), version == the owner's real bump target. AC-007 [UNCHANGED, still valid per spec revision_note]: owner with two platform siblings, both real, disk-discovered GroupMember::PlatformManifest members (e.g. linux-x64-gnu and darwin-arm64 targets), both bumped -- plan_version's platform_writes contains one PlatformWrite entry per platform member (two entries total), each with its own manifest path and matching from/version values.
test.expected_failure: plan_version_platform_write_from_resolves_cargo_workspace_inherited_version: since TASK-2 already landed and its loop is agnostic to how a GroupMember::PlatformManifest entered ws.config.groups.fixed (real walk discovery or direct fixture construction), this test is expected to pass immediately once written. A failure here means TASK-2's loop forwarded `member.role` into `ManifestDecl::new` instead of hardcoding `ManifestRole::Canonical` (commands/version.rs line 300) -- which would surface as `Err(GraphError::Manifest(ManifestError::...))` from the Platform-role-vs-CargoToml-format rejection at callisto-model/src/package.rs:104-106 instead of `Ok(..)` with one PlatformWrite entry. plan_version_emits_platform_write_for_each_of_two_platform_siblings fails before TASK-2's implementation lands (platform_writes hardcoded empty); after TASK-2, it should already pass with zero further implementation changes -- a failure means only one platform member is being processed, or cargo_workspace inheritance isn't reaching the correct WorkspaceInheritance.

implementation.description: No new implementation code -- TASK-2's landed loop (commands/version.rs lines 282-330) already iterates every PlatformManifest member per group regardless of how it entered ws.config.groups.fixed, already hardcodes ManifestRole::Canonical unconditionally (line 300, ignoring member.role), and already derives cargo_workspace/open_ctx from the real workspace root (lines 264-280). This task exists purely to pin AC-002b's corrected fixture-based scenario and AC-007's unchanged two-sibling scenario with dedicated tests.
steps: No production code changes. If plan_version_platform_write_from_resolves_cargo_workspace_inherited_version fails, the bug is TASK-2's loop forwarding member.role into ManifestDecl::new instead of hardcoding ManifestRole::Canonical in commands/version.rs's platform_writes loop -- fix that.

No production code changes. If plan_version_emits_platform_write_for_each_of_two_platform_siblings fails, the bug is TASK-2's loop only processing the first PlatformManifest member found per group, or cargo_workspace being derived as None instead of from WorkspaceCargoResolver -- fix that in commands/version.rs rather than adding new code here.

implementation.description: Extend the loop added in Task 2 to also detect a matching optional dependency on the owner's canonical manifest and accumulate updates per owner-manifest-path (using a BTreeMap so multiple platform siblings under the same owner naturally merge, which Task 6 pins).
steps: In the same loop from Task 2, also bind `name` from the GroupMember::PlatformManifest destructure.
Before the loop, add a `BTreeMap<PathBuf, Vec<(String, Version)>>` accumulator for optional dep updates.

Resolve `owner: PackageId` to its Package via the existing `pkg_map: HashMap<&PackageId, &Package>` (commands/version.rs, built earlier in plan_version). Call `.canonical_manifests()` on that Package (crates/callisto-model/src/package.rs:24-28, an iterator since dual-published packages like npm+Cargo can have more than one). Rule: if it yields more than one canonical manifest, use only the FIRST one returned -- Fixed-group owners with platform-manifest siblings are expected to be single-ecosystem in practice, and this track does not add multi-manifest optional-dependency-update logic (out of scope per the spec's non_goals on new planning-logic paths). Then open that manifest and check via iter_dependencies() whether an existing DepKind::Optional entry matches the platform member's name.
After the loop, convert the accumulator into Vec<OptionalDepUpdate> and assign it to the VersionPlan struct literal's `optional_dep_updates` field, replacing `Vec::new()`.

tasks.title: apply.rs Fix 1: extend active_ecosystems to platform_writes and optional_dep_updates manifest paths
tasks.reasoning: active_ecosystems (apply.rs:325-349) currently only derives from plan.bumps, so a plan with only platform_writes/optional_dep_updates populated (bumps empty) never stages the npm lockfile even though an npm manifest was touched. This task extends the same active_ecosystems HashSet-building expression to also fold in plan.platform_writes and plan.optional_dep_updates manifest paths via ManifestFormat::from_path(...).ecosystem(). This task is independent of Tasks 1-6 (different file, does not touch PlatformWrite's fields) and independent of Task 8 (no precondition logic involved) -- it can be built and merged in any order relative to them.

test.description: AC-009 (platform_writes-only plan stages the npm lockfile, no refresh), AC-010 (same for optional_dep_updates-only plan), AC-011 (bumps-only plan behavior is a byte-for-byte regression -- already covered by every pre-existing apply.rs test in this file, which all currently pass and must continue to pass unmodified).
test.expected_failure: Both tests fail: `assert!(outcome.staged.contains(...))` fails because active_ecosystems is currently derived only from plan.bumps (empty in both plans), so Ecosystem::Npm is never in the set and the lockfile is skipped in the staging loop at apply.rs:423-431.

implementation.description: Extend the active_ecosystems HashSet-building code (apply.rs:325-349) to also fold in manifest paths from plan.platform_writes and plan.optional_dep_updates.
steps: In crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs, chain two additional filter_map iterators onto the existing active_ecosystems collect(): one over plan.platform_writes mapping each pw.manifest through ManifestFormat::from_path(...).ok().map(|fmt| fmt.ecosystem()), and one over plan.optional_dep_updates doing the same for opt.manifest.

No other code changes -- the existing lockfile_ecosystems staging table (apply.rs:412-422) and refresh-subprocess logic (apply.rs:354-408) are untouched, since npm has no refresh subprocess and Cargo/Pypi refresh triggers stay scoped to plan.bumps-driven ecosystems only.

tasks.expected_pass: all tests pass, including all pre-existing apply.rs tests (proving AC-011's byte-for-byte regression requirement)
tasks.commit_message:
fix(graph): stage npm lockfile when a plan touches only platform_writes or optional_dep_updates

active_ecosystems previously derived exclusively from plan.bumps, so a plan containing only platform-manifest or optional-dependency writes never staged the npm lockfile. Extends the derivation to also consult those two fields' manifest paths.

tasks.title: apply.rs Fix 2: platform_writes dispatch loop precondition check
tasks.reasoning: The platform_writes dispatch loop (apply.rs:244-252) currently writes unconditionally with no precondition check, unlike the sibling bump loops which already check current==from/current==target/else. This task adds the same three-way branch using PlatformWrite.from (added in Task 1), returning GraphError::UnexpectedManifestVersion on drift, treating current==target as idempotent-retry success.

test.description: Three tests: AC-012 (drift -- current is neither from nor target -> Err(UnexpectedManifestVersion) with correct fields, manifest not written), AC-012b (current already equals target -> Ok, no re-write, but path still pushed to staged), AC-013 (current equals from, the ordinary case -> succeeds, on-disk version becomes target -- this is the pre-existing test from apply.rs:2240, already updated with a matching `from` in Task 1, and must continue to pass unmodified as the regression proof).
test.expected_failure: platform_write_drift_returns_unexpected_manifest_version_and_leaves_manifest_untouched fails: `apply_version_plan` currently succeeds unconditionally (writes 1.1.0 over the drifted 9.9.9), so `result` is `Ok(..)` not `Err(UnexpectedManifestVersion)`, and the manifest is NOT unchanged. platform_write_idempotent_retry_when_already_at_target_succeeds_without_rewrite happens to pass even before the fix (current unconditional-write behavior also succeeds here), but is included to pin AC-012b's exact non-error semantics once the precondition check exists.

implementation.description: Add the same three-way current==from/current==to/else branch the sibling bump loops already use, to the platform_writes dispatch loop.
steps: In crates/callisto-graph/src/apply.rs, in the platform_writes loop (currently around lines 244-252), after opening the handle, read current_version(), then branch: if current == pw.version, skip the write (idempotent retry) but still push to modified_paths; else if current == pw.from, write_version + persist as before; else, return Err(GraphError::UnexpectedManifestVersion { path: pw.manifest.clone(), expected_from: pw.from.clone(), expected_to: pw.version.clone(), found: current }).

tasks.expected_pass: all tests pass, including the pre-existing apply_version_plan_executes_platform_writes_and_optional_dep_updates test (proving AC-013's non-drifted regression path)
tasks.commit_message:
fix(graph): add current-version precondition check to platform_writes dispatch loop

apply_version_plan previously wrote platform manifests unconditionally, unlike the sibling bump loops. Adds the same current==from/current==to/else precondition, returning UnexpectedManifestVersion on drift and treating current==to as a safe idempotent-retry success.
